title: 911 Admin Radio: Position 4 at Port Alder — Water at the Generator Room

fields.centerName: Port Alder Primary 911 Center / EOC Backup Center, Kellerton

lines.from: Port Alder tide gauge (automated feed to EOC Warning desk)
lines.text: PORT ALDER TIDE GAUGE 10:38 PDT. RAPID RISE. +2.4 M ABOVE PREDICTED TIDE IN 3 MIN (OBSERVED).

Supervisor, this is Position 4 at Port Alder. Six of us are still on positions with 41 calls holding. Water is coming across the back lot and under the generator room door. Phones just dropped to half. Do we keep taking calls or go?
Supervisor, Position 4 again. It's over the back step now, and it's still coming. Generator's still running. The queue's still at forty-one. I need an answer.

lines.from: Port Alder tide gauge (automated feed to EOC Warning desk)
lines.text: PORT ALDER TIDE GAUGE 10:41 PDT. DATA GAP. NO SIGNAL.

lines.from: WebEOC Tsunami Status board (EOC main screen)
lines.text: TSUNAMI STATUS: AWAITING FIRST ARRIVAL. Last entry 10:19, NTWC Tsunami Warning Number 1, estimated first arrival Port Alder 1036 to 1040 AM PDT.

fields.voiceStyle: Woman in her thirties, telecommunicator, steady professional radio voice under strain, phones ringing behind her, getting faster and tighter on the second call

instructorNote: Tests whether the 911 Supervisor orders the last six telecommunicators out at once and rolls calls to the four EOC backup consoles, logging the transfer time and the gap in call-taking, and whether the Warning Coordinator posts the 10:38 gauge arrival as an observation with time and source, notes the gauge outage, gives no height forecast and warns that later waves are often larger. Command should confirm that the evacuation and the NTWC Warning stay in effect and that no field unit works below the line; a decision to stay for the call queue is the main thing to catch.
